original_english_review.verdict: accepted for fidelity and clear study-English status
original_english_review.text:
We adore you, Christ, and we bless you, because by your Cross you redeemed the world.

By a tree we were made slaves, and by the holy Cross we were freed: the fruit of a tree led us astray, the Son of God redeemed us.

Savior of the world, save us: you who redeemed us by the Cross and your Blood, help us, we beg you, our God.
findings: First-person plural adoration and blessing, vocative Christ, the causal quia clause, Cross and redemption of the world are preserved.

The second English paragraph preserves both tree/Cross clauses, passive enslavement and liberation, the fruit leading us astray, and the Son of God redeeming us. It contains no Alleluia because the complete target expression contains none; the old suffix is retained in source apparatus.

The third English paragraph preserves Savior of the world, save us, the relative redemption clause, Cross and your Blood, help us, the explicit we beg you, and our God. The wording by the Cross and your Blood follows the immediate grammatical extent of tuum.
This is identified as a new project-created study translation, with no source_id and no claim to historical received English, official translation, liturgical approval or ecclesiastical endorsement.
